records.title: How to Report a Pothole
records.description: Step-by-step guide to reporting potholes and what happens after you submit.
records.content:
Potholes are one of the most commonly reported issues in our city. Here's everything you need to know about reporting them and what to expect.

## What Qualifies as a Pothole?
A pothole is a depression or hole in the road surface, typically caused by water erosion and traffic wear. They can range from small dips to large, tire-damaging holes.

## How to Report
1. Note the exact location (address or nearest intersection)
2. Estimate the size (small: < 1 ft, medium: 1-2 ft, large: > 2 ft)
3. Take a photo if it's safe to do so
4. Submit through our Service Request form

## What Happens Next
- Your report is reviewed within 24 hours
- A crew is dispatched based on severity and location
- Most potholes are repaired within 5 business days
- You'll receive status updates via email

## Emergency Potholes
If a pothole poses an immediate safety hazard (very deep, on a highway, or causing accidents), call 311 directly for emergency dispatch.

records.title: Waste Collection Schedule & Guidelines
records.description: Everything about garbage, recycling, and green bin collection days and rules.
records.content:
Keep our city clean by following waste collection guidelines.

## Collection Schedule
Collection occurs weekly on your designated day. Check your address online to confirm your specific collection day.

## What Goes Where?

### Garbage (Gray Bin)
- Non-recyclable packaging
- Disposable diapers
- Broken ceramics/pottery
- Pet waste (bagged)

### Recycling (Blue Bin)
- Paper, cardboard, newspaper
- Plastic containers (#1-7)
- Glass bottles and jars
- Metal cans and aluminum

### Green Bin (Organics)
- Food scraps and leftovers
- Coffee grounds and filters
- Yard waste (small quantities)
- Paper towels and napkins

## Important Rules
- Bins must be at the curb by 7:00 AM
- Bins should be removed from curb by 7:00 PM
- Do not overfill bins — lids must close completely
- Contaminated recycling loads will not be collected

records.title: Understanding Your Water Bill
records.description: A guide to reading your water bill and understanding charges.
records.content:
Your water bill may seem complicated, but here's a breakdown of what each section means.

## Bill Components
1. **Water Usage Charge** — Based on your metered consumption in cubic meters
2. **Wastewater Charge** — Calculated as a percentage of water usage
3. **Stormwater Charge** — Flat rate based on your property size
4. **Service Charge** — Fixed monthly charge for infrastructure maintenance

## Reading Your Meter
Your water meter measures consumption in cubic meters. One cubic meter equals 1,000 liters — roughly 10 bathtub fills.

## High Bill?
If your bill seems unusually high:
- Check for running toilets (put food coloring in the tank)
- Inspect for dripping faucets
- Check outdoor hoses and irrigation
- Review if you had guests or changed routines

## Payment Options
Pay online, by phone, at city hall, or set up automatic payments.

records.title: Tree Maintenance on City Property
records.description: Who is responsible for trees and how to request city tree maintenance.
records.content:
The city maintains over 200,000 trees on public property. Here's what you need to know.

## City Responsibility
The city maintains trees on:
- City boulevards (between the sidewalk and road)
- Parks and green spaces
- City-owned properties and facilities

## Your Responsibility
Property owners are responsible for:
- Trees on their private property
- Removing leaves and fruit from city trees that fall on their property
- Not damaging city trees (trimming, removing, or poisoning city trees is an offence)

## When to Report
Report a city tree if it:
- Has a broken or hanging branch
- Is leaning dangerously
- Shows signs of disease (unusual spots, decay)
- Is dead or dying
- Has roots damaging sidewalks

## Emergency
If a tree has fallen and is blocking a road or threatening a structure, call 311 immediately.

records.title: Noise By-law: What You Need to Know
records.description: Understand noise regulations, quiet hours, and how to file a complaint.
records.content:
Our noise by-law ensures everyone can enjoy a reasonable level of quiet in their neighbourhood.

## Quiet Hours
- **Weekdays**: 11:00 PM to 7:00 AM
- **Weekends/Holidays**: 11:00 PM to 9:00 AM

## Construction Hours
- **Weekdays**: 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM
- **Saturdays**: 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM
- **Sundays/Holidays**: No construction permitted

## What's Covered
The by-law covers:
- Loud music and amplified sound
- Construction noise outside permitted hours
- Persistent barking dogs
- Loud parties
- Commercial vehicle noise
- Power tools outside permitted hours

## Filing a Complaint
Noise complaints are most effective when noise is actively occurring. Include the source address, type of noise, and duration.

records.title: How Street Light Repairs Work
records.description: Learn how to report a streetlight issue and what the repair process involves.
records.content:
Well-maintained street lighting is essential for public safety.

## Identifying Your Streetlight
Most streetlight poles have an identification number on a small plate about 6 feet up. This number helps crews locate the exact light.

## Common Issues
- **Out completely** — bulb failure or electrical issue
- **Flickering** — often a bulb nearing end of life
- **On during the day** — photocell malfunction
- **Buzzing** — ballast issue
- **Leaning pole** — potential safety hazard (call 311 immediately)

## Repair Timeline
- Standard repairs: 5 business days
- Safety hazards: 24-48 hours
- Major electrical work: may require longer

## LED Conversion
The city is converting all streetlights to LED. LED lights are brighter, more efficient, and last 3-4 times longer than traditional bulbs.

records.title: Graffiti Prevention & Removal
records.description: How the city handles graffiti and what property owners can do.
records.content:
Graffiti removal keeps our community looking its best and discourages further vandalism.

## City Graffiti Removal
The city removes graffiti from:
- City-owned buildings and infrastructure
- Bridges, overpasses, and retaining walls
- Utility boxes and transit shelters
- Private property visible from public space (with owner consent)

## Response Time
Most graffiti is removed within 5 business days of being reported. Offensive content is prioritized for faster removal.

## Prevention Tips
- Apply anti-graffiti coatings to vulnerable surfaces
- Improve lighting around your property
- Plant thorny bushes near walls
- Install security cameras
- Report graffiti promptly (quick removal discourages repeat vandalism)

## Reporting
Photos are required when reporting graffiti so crews can assess the surface type and prepare appropriate removal methods.

records.title: Requesting an Event Permit
records.description: Guide to obtaining permits for community events, festivals, and gatherings.
records.content:
Planning a community event? Here's what you need to know about permits.

## When Do You Need a Permit?
- Events in city parks with 50+ attendees
- Events requiring road closures
- Events with amplified sound
- Events serving food to the public
- Fundraising events on city property

## Application Timeline
- **Small events** (< 100 people): Apply 30 days in advance
- **Medium events** (100-500): Apply 60 days in advance
- **Large events** (500+): Apply 90 days in advance

## Fees
Permit fees vary based on:
- Event size and duration
- City services required (road closures, garbage, etc.)
- Whether the event is commercial or non-profit

## Insurance
Most events require proof of liability insurance ($2 million minimum) naming the city as additional insured.

records.title: Traffic Calming: Requesting Measures for Your Street
records.description: How to request speed bumps, crosswalks, or other traffic calming on your street.
records.content:
If you're concerned about speeding or pedestrian safety on your street, you can request traffic calming measures.

## What Is Traffic Calming?
Traffic calming includes physical measures to slow vehicle speeds and improve safety:
- Speed humps/bumps
- Curb extensions (bump-outs)
- Raised crosswalks
- Traffic circles
- Reduced speed zones

## How to Request
1. Submit a Traffic Calming Request form
2. A traffic study will be conducted
3. Results are reviewed against criteria
4. If approved, measures are scheduled for installation

## Evaluation Criteria
- Traffic speed data (85th percentile)
- Traffic volume
- Collision history
- Proximity to schools, parks, seniors' facilities
- Pedestrian and cyclist counts

## Timeline
Traffic studies take 20-30 business days. Installation, if approved, depends on budget and scheduling.

records.title: Winter Road Maintenance Guide
records.description: How the city handles snow clearing, salting, and winter road safety.
records.content:
Our winter maintenance program keeps roads and sidewalks safe during winter months.

## Plowing Priority
1. **Priority 1**: Highways, arterial roads, transit routes, hospital access
2. **Priority 2**: Collector roads, school zones
3. **Priority 3**: Residential streets
4. **Priority 4**: Cul-de-sacs, dead-end streets

## Timeline After Snowfall
- Priority 1 roads: Within 4 hours
- Priority 2 roads: Within 8 hours
- Priority 3-4 roads: Within 24 hours
- Sidewalks: Within 24 hours

## Your Responsibilities
- Clear your sidewalk within 24 hours after snowfall
- Don't push snow onto the road or neighbour's property
- Keep fire hydrants near your property clear
- Don't park on the street during snow events if possible

## Salt & Sand
The city uses a mix of salt and sand on roads. We monitor temperatures and adjust the mix for effectiveness while minimizing environmental impact.

records.title: How to Request a New Waste Bin
records.description: Guide to requesting new, replacement, or additional waste bins for your property.
records.content:
Need a new waste bin? Here's what you need to know.

## Standard Bins
Each residential property receives:
- 1 garbage bin (gray)
- 1 recycling bin (blue)
- 1 green bin (green)

## Replacement Bins
If your bin is damaged or stolen:
- Report it through the Service Request form
- Replacement bins are delivered within 7 business days
- No charge for first replacement

## Additional Bins
- Additional garbage bins: $75/year
- Additional recycling bins: Free
- Downsizing to a smaller garbage bin: Credit on your utility bill

## Bin Sizes
- Small: 80L (single person/couple)
- Standard: 120L (average household)
- Large: 240L (larger families)

records.title: Parking Rules & Common Violations
records.description: Overview of city parking regulations and how to avoid tickets.
records.content:
Understanding parking rules can help you avoid fines and keep traffic flowing.

## General Rules
- Maximum 3-hour parking on city streets (unless signed otherwise)
- No parking within 1.5 meters of a driveway
- No parking within 3 meters of a fire hydrant
- No parking on sidewalks or boulevards

## Common Violations
1. Expired meter
2. Overtime parking
3. No parking zone
4. Blocking a driveway
5. Fire route

## Disputing a Ticket
You have 15 days to dispute a parking ticket:
- Online through the city's ticket dispute portal
- In person at City Hall
- By mail with a written explanation

## Winter Parking Ban
During declared snow events, overnight street parking may be banned to allow plowing.

records.title: Dealing with Wildlife in Your Neighbourhood
records.description: Tips for coexisting with urban wildlife and when to call for help.
records.content:
As our city grows, wildlife interactions become more common. Here's how to stay safe.

## Common Urban Wildlife
- Raccoons, skunks, and squirrels
- Coyotes
- Canada geese
- Deer (in some areas)
- Various bird species

## Prevention
- Secure garbage and compost bins
- Don't leave pet food outdoors
- Remove bird feeders if attracting unwanted wildlife
- Seal entry points to attics and sheds
- Keep small pets supervised outdoors

## When to Report
Contact Animal Services if:
- An animal appears sick or injured
- A coyote is approaching people/pets
- An animal is trapped
- You find a wild animal in your home

## Do NOT
- Feed wild animals
- Approach or corner wildlife
- Attempt to capture animals yourself
- Use poison (illegal and dangerous)

records.title: Accessibility in City Services
records.description: How the city ensures accessibility and how to request accommodations.
records.content:
Our city is committed to providing accessible services for all residents.

## Accessible Services
- All city buildings have wheelchair access
- ASL interpretation available for council meetings
- Documents available in alternative formats
- TTY/relay service for phone inquiries
- Accessible transit options

## Requesting Accommodations
If you need an accommodation for a city service or event:
1. Contact us at least 2 weeks in advance
2. Describe the accommodation needed
3. We will work with you to find a solution

## Reporting Barriers
If you encounter an accessibility barrier:
- Broken accessible buttons or ramps
- Inaccessible city websites or documents
- Service counters that aren't accessible
- Missing tactile indicators

## Feedback
We welcome feedback on how to improve accessibility. Your input helps us identify and remove barriers.

records.title: Property Standards: What Owners Need to Know
records.description: Minimum property maintenance standards and how to stay compliant.
records.content:
All properties in the city must meet minimum maintenance standards.

## Key Requirements
- **Yard**: Grass under 8 inches, no noxious weeds
- **Structure**: No broken windows, peeling paint, or damaged siding
- **Fences**: Must be in good repair, not leaning
- **Driveways**: No large cracks or trip hazards
- **Storage**: No junk, debris, or inoperable vehicles visible

## Enforcement Process
1. Complaint received or proactive inspection
2. Property owner notified with compliance deadline
3. Re-inspection after deadline
4. If not compliant: fines and/or city remediation at owner's expense

## Appeal
Property owners can appeal a standards notice within 14 days of receiving it.

## Resources
- Low-income property owners may qualify for repair grants
- Seniors can access volunteer yard maintenance programs

records.title: How 311 Service Requests Are Processed
records.description: Behind the scenes: how your 311 request moves from submission to resolution.
records.content:
Ever wonder what happens after you submit a 311 request? Here's the journey.

## The Process

### 1. Submitted
Your request enters our system and receives a unique tracking ID (SR-XXXX-YYYYMMDD).

### 2. Reviewed/Triaged
A 311 coordinator reviews your request, confirms the category, and sets priority based on urgency and impact.

### 3. Assigned
The request is routed to the appropriate city department and assigned to a team or individual.

### 4. In Progress
The assigned team investigates and works on resolving the issue. You may receive updates during this phase.

### 5. Resolved
The issue has been addressed. You'll receive a notification with details of what was done.

### 6. Closed
After resolution is confirmed (either by you or after a waiting period), the request is closed.

## Tracking Your Request
Use your Request ID and email to track status anytime through our Track page.

records.title: Fire Hydrant Maintenance & Reporting
records.description: Why fire hydrants matter and how to report issues.
records.content:
Fire hydrants are critical infrastructure that can save lives and property.

## Maintenance Schedule
The city inspects and tests all fire hydrants annually, including:
- Flow testing
- Painting and visibility
- Operability checks
- Winterizing (draining) before freezing weather

## Resident Responsibilities
- Keep hydrants near your property clear of snow (1-meter radius)
- Don't plant shrubs or place objects near hydrants
- Report any damage, leaks, or obstructions immediately
- Never park in front of a hydrant

## Report Issues
Report a fire hydrant that is:
- Leaking or spraying water
- Hit by a vehicle
- Buried in snow/vegetation
- Missing a cap
- Painted an incorrect color

## Hydrant Colors
Did you know hydrant colors indicate flow rate? Yellow = high flow, green = moderate, red = low flow.

records.title: Illegal Dumping: Penalties & Reporting
records.description: How to report illegal dumping and the penalties for offenders.
records.content:
Illegal dumping harms our environment and costs taxpayers.

## What Is Illegal Dumping?
Illegal dumping is disposing of waste outside designated facilities, including:
- Construction debris on vacant lots
- Household garbage in parks or waterways
- Tires, appliances, or furniture on public land
- Commercial waste in residential bins

## Penalties
- Individuals: Fines from $500 to $10,000
- Companies: Fines from $2,000 to $50,000
- Repeat offenders: Increased fines and potential prosecution

## How to Report
1. Note the exact location
2. Describe what was dumped
3. Take photos (safely, from a distance)
4. Note any identifying information (if a vehicle was involved)
5. Submit through our reporting form

## Proper Disposal
- City transfer stations accept most materials
- Hazardous waste collection events held quarterly
- Large item pickup available for residents

records.title: Sidewalk Safety: Winter Ice and Trip Hazards
records.description: Your responsibilities for sidewalk maintenance and how to report hazards.
records.content:
Safe sidewalks are a shared responsibility between the city and property owners.

## Property Owner Responsibilities
- Clear ice and snow from adjacent sidewalks within 24 hours
- Apply salt or sand on icy patches
- Ensure walkways to your door are clear
- Maintain sidewalks on your property

## City Responsibilities
- Repair damaged public sidewalks
- Maintain pedestrian crossings
- Clear sidewalks on city property
- Priority sidewalk plowing near schools and transit

## Reporting Hazards
Report sidewalk hazards that include:
- Large cracks or heaves
- Missing or broken sections
- Persistent ice patches
- Obstructions blocking the path

## Liability
Property owners can be held liable for injuries caused by uncleared ice or snow on sidewalks adjacent to their property.

records.title: Community Recreation Programs
records.description: Overview of city recreation programs, registration, and financial assistance.
records.content:
The city offers hundreds of recreation programs for all ages and abilities.

## Programs Available
- Swimming lessons and aquafit
- Youth sports leagues
- Seniors' fitness and social programs
- Arts and crafts classes
- Day camps (summer and PA days)
- Drop-in activities

## Registration
- Online registration opens seasonally
- In-person registration at community centres
- Phone registration available

## Financial Assistance
Can't afford the fees? The city offers:
- **Fee Assistance Program**: Subsidized or free registration
- **Equipment lending**: Free equipment loans
- **Drop-in programs**: Many free drop-in options

## Facility Bookings
Need space for a private event? Community centre rooms, fields, and pools can be booked through our facilities team.

records.title: Sewer Backup Prevention
records.description: How to prevent sewer backups and what to do if one occurs.
records.content:
Sewer backups can cause significant property damage. Here's how to prevent them.

## Prevention
- Install a backwater valve ($1,000-$3,000 — city offers subsidies)
- Don't pour grease down drains
- Don't flush wipes (even "flushable" ones)
- Clear debris from floor drains regularly
- Know where your sewer cleanout is located

## Warning Signs
- Slow draining in multiple fixtures
- Gurgling sounds from drains
- Water backing up in basement
- Sewage odors

## If a Backup Occurs
1. Stop using water immediately
2. Call 311 to report
3. Document damage with photos
4. Contact a licensed plumber
5. Contact your insurance company

## City Rebate Program
The city offers rebates up to $3,000 for backwater valve installation.

records.title: Housing Support Programs
records.description: Overview of affordable housing, rent assistance, and emergency shelter resources.
records.content:
The city provides a range of housing support services for residents in need.

## Emergency Shelter
- 24/7 emergency shelter intake line
- Emergency family shelter beds
- Warming centres during extreme cold alerts

## Rent Assistance
- **Rent Supplement Program**: Monthly assistance for eligible households
- **Housing Allowance**: Financial assistance for low-income renters
- **Utility Assistance**: Help with utility arrears

## Affordable Housing
- Centralized waitlist for all affordable housing
- Priority categories: seniors, families, persons with disabilities
- Average wait: 7-12 years (varies by category)

## Homelessness Prevention
- Eviction prevention assistance
- Financial counselling
- Emergency financial assistance
- Landlord mediation services

## How to Apply
Contact our Housing Services team by phone, in person, or through a service request.

records.title: Reporting Abandoned Vehicles
records.description: How to identify and report abandoned vehicles on city streets.
records.content:
Abandoned vehicles can be safety hazards and eyesores. Here's how the city handles them.

## What Qualifies?
A vehicle may be considered abandoned if:
- Parked on the street for 7+ consecutive days
- No license plates or expired plates
- Flat tires or obviously inoperable
- Appears to be derelict

## Reporting
When reporting, try to include:
- Exact location
- Vehicle make, model, color
- License plate number (if present)
- How long you've noticed it
- Photos

## Process
1. By-law officer investigates within 7 days
2. Warning tag placed on vehicle (48-hour notice)
3. If not removed, vehicle is towed to impound
4. Owner has 14 days to claim before disposal

## Note
Vehicles on private property are handled differently — contact By-law Enforcement for guidance.

records.title: Food Safety & Community Food Programs
records.description: Find local food banks, community kitchens, and nutrition programs.
records.content:
No one in our city should go hungry. Here's how to access food support.

## Food Banks
The city partners with food banks across all wards. Find your nearest location:
- Most open 2-3 days per week
- Bring ID and proof of address
- No appointment needed at most locations

## Community Meals
- Free hot meals at community centres
- Senior lunch programs
- After-school snack programs
- Community kitchen programs (learn to cook!)

## Emergency Food
- Same-day emergency food hampers available
- Call 311 to be connected to nearest provider

## School Nutrition
- Breakfast and lunch programs in schools
- Snack programs for elementary students
- Summer nutrition programs

## Donate
Want to help? Food banks accept:
- Non-perishable food items
- Cash donations (they can buy more efficiently)
- Volunteer time

records.title: What to Do in a City Emergency
records.description: Essential information for city emergencies: floods, power outages, and severe weather.
records.content:
Being prepared for emergencies helps keep you and your family safe.

## Emergency Contacts
- **911**: Life-threatening emergencies
- **311**: Non-emergency city services
- **Poison Control**: 1-800-268-9017
- **City Emergency Hotline**: Active during declared emergencies

## Types of Emergencies

### Flooding
- Move valuables above basement level
- Don't walk or drive through floodwater
- Report flooding to 311
- Check on elderly neighbours

### Power Outages
- Report to your utility provider
- Keep fridge/freezer closed
- Use flashlights, not candles
- Check on vulnerable neighbours

### Severe Weather
- Monitor Environment Canada alerts
- Seek shelter in interior rooms
- Stay away from windows

## Emergency Preparedness
Every household should have:
- 72-hour emergency kit
- Battery-powered radio
- Flashlights and extra batteries
- First aid kit
- Copies of important documents
- Cash (ATMs may not work)
